title: How Large Language Models Misrepresent American Climate Opinions
abstract: arXiv:2512.23889v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate public opinion, standing in for survey respondents as "silicon samples." Whether they faithfully represent U.S. climate opinion, particularly at the intersections of race, gender, and ideology, remains largely untested. We prompted six large language models with the profiles of 978 respondents to a nationally representative U.S. climate opinion survey and compared the generated responses with those respondents' own answers across 20 questions. The models compress the diversity of American climate opinion, pulling predictions toward the population mean: less-concerned groups are predicted as more concerned, more-concerned groups as less, and the variance of predicted responses falls, on average, 29% below that of human responses. translated_title: 大语言模型如何歪曲美国气候民意
translated_abstract: 大语言模型越来越多地被用于模拟公众舆论，作为“硅基样本”替代调查受访者。然而，它们能否忠实呈现美国气候民意，特别是在种族、性别和意识形态的交叉维度上，在很大程度上仍未得到检验。我们以一项具有全国代表性的美国气候民意调查中978名受访者的画像作为提示，输入六个大语言模型，并将模型生成的回答与这些受访者本人在20个问题上的真实回答进行比较。研究发现，这些模型压缩了美国气候舆论的多样性，将预测拉向人口总体均值：关注度较低的群体被预测为更加关注气候，而关注度较高的群体则被预测为关注较少，预测回答的方差平均比人类真实回答低29%。这种压缩呈现出交叉性特征：模型套用了单一的性别假设，在所有种族群体中都预测女性比男性更支持气候行动。
tldr: 研究发现大语言模型在模拟美国气候民意时系统性地压缩观点多样性，将预测拉向人口均值并套用刻板的性别假设，在种族与性别交叉维度上尤其失真。
en_tdlr: Large language models systematically compress the diversity of American climate opinion by pulling predictions toward the population mean and applying uniform gender assumptions, particularly misrepresenting opinions at the intersections of race and gender.
